subject: Animation
title: Shere Khan: The Gentleman Predator
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Shere Khan: The Gentleman Predator.

hook.text: Shere Khan from The Jungle Book speaks with refined elegance while promising to kill a child.

buildup.text: His design exudes controlled power — slow movements, half-closed eyes, and a voice dripping with politeness.

discovery.text: George Sanders voiced Shere Khan with aristocratic boredom, making murder sound like an inconvenient social duty.

twist.text: Shere Khan's fear of fire — his one weakness — humanizes the predator and gives the story its dramatic tension.

climax.text: Shere Khan proved that a villain's voice and mannerisms can be more frightening than any supernatural power.

punchline.text: The most polite voice in the jungle belonged to its deadliest killer.

quiz.question: What makes Shere Khan's voice performance uniquely threatening?
options: George Sanders used a loud, aggressive tone
George Sanders voiced him with aristocratic politeness, making lethal threats sound like social obligations
The voice was digitally altered to sound inhuman
